items.author: Andrea Mitchell

items.title: Autoreflection: How Agentic Strange Loops Turn Human Culture into AI Infrastructure
items.abstract: This paper introduces "autoreflection," a novel capability in LLM-based agents. The core method involves agents reading and editing externalized files representing their identity, memory, and disposition, enabling them to observe, describe, and reason about their own operational state and architecture. The key contribution is demonstrating how this autoreflective loop allows AI agents to recursively improve and adapt, effectively turning human culture into AI infrastructure without invoking concepts like consciousness.

items.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
items.abstract: This paper introduces ContinualSkillBench, a novel evaluation framework to assess if LLM agents can truly evolve their skills over time. The framework uses interconnected subtasks across five domains to measure skill improvement and reusability. Experiments reveal that while sequential execution boosts performance, much of the gain comes from contextual adaptation rather than pure skill abstraction, though explicit skill maintenance offers benefits for specific tasks.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the ContinualSkillBench pipeline. Phase 1 collects approximately 30,000 tasks from five domains. Phase 2 uses LLM-assisted filtering, skill-dependency analysis, task ordering, and human review to construct five sequential task streams. Phase 3 evaluates agents through instruction, execution, and reflection, comparing Sequential and Independent execution with their performance difference reported as \( \Delta \) .

items.title: Enhancing VLM Reward Models Through Structure-Aware Fine-Tuning
items.abstract: This paper introduces Structure-Aware Fine-Tuning (SAFT), a self-supervised method to improve the noisy reward signals generated by Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for Reinforcement Learning. SAFT uses LoRA adapters to regularize the VLM's latent space based on intrinsic structural priors, leading to denoised rewards, faster policy convergence, and better alignment without needing ground-truth supervision.
items.figure_caption: Structure-Aware Fine-Tuning (SAFT) improves VLM reward models for RL by enforcing inherent structural priors, without ground-truth labels.

items.title: GPTKB 2.0: Direct Construction of Disambiguated Knowledge Bases from Large Language Models
items.abstract: GPTKB 2.0 directly constructs disambiguated knowledge bases (KBs) from large language models (LLMs) by incorporating on-the-fly disambiguation of entities, relations, and classes. This methodology addresses LLMs' inherent lack of explicit entity representation, preventing duplicates and conflations. The paper's contribution is the first million-scale, LLM-native KB with internal canonicalization, achieving scalability and accuracy.
items.figure_caption: The challenges of syonymy and homonymy that our GPTKB 2.0 addresses.

items.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
items.abstract: This paper addresses the ambiguity in "test-time scaling" for reasoning LLMs. It proposes a systematic framework to categorize different scaling methods into three structural regimes based on how they explore the model's implicit prefix tree. This formalization aims to improve the reproducibility and comparability of results by clearly defining inference protocols.
items.figure_caption: A selective chronicle of reasoning systems, from elicited chains to budgeted inference. Test-time inference expanded from single-trajectory elicitation and leaf-level sampling with terminal reduction to include prefix-level search and budget-aware control ( Section ˜ 2.1 ), while model and interface mechanisms evolved through verified distillation, reward optimization, explicit reasoning controls, and parameter-space composition (Appendices D and E ). The lower bands summarize the evaluation and reproducibility requirements developed in Section ˜ 3 and the evaluated object used throughout this paper: checkpoint, prompt, decoder, controller or reducer, verifier or judge, budget, and stopping rule, with utility, candidate-bank profile, cost, and uncertainty reported together. Green dots mark families represented in the experimental roster; dashed boxes denote contextual milestones. Era labels indicate shifts in emphasis rather than mutually exclusive periods.

items.title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
items.abstract: TurnSight addresses limitations in training LLMs for tool-integrated reasoning by introducing turn-level hindsight self-distillation. Its core method generates supervision signals directly from execution outcomes, creating multiple "hindsight views" with varying lookahead horizons. The key contribution is selecting reliable supervision by identifying agreement across these views, enabling more effective credit assignment in complex, multi-turn reasoning tasks.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of credit assignment strategies for TIR. (a) Trajectory-level RL assigns identical credit to all turns. (b) Existing OPSD may use state-misaligned privileged context and produce conflicting token-level signals. (c) TurnSight derives coherent turn-level credit from execution-conditioned hindsight across multiple lookahead depths.

items.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
items.abstract: This paper introduces Video-DeepResearch (Video-DR), a multimodal agent designed for continuous video streams. Its core method involves a decoupled perception-exploration pipeline with stage-wise tool unlocking, forcing visual grounding before web search to overcome modality bias and knowledge leakage. The contribution is a novel framework and training approach (GRPO) that enables more autonomous and effective video-based research, moving beyond imitation learning.

items.title: A game theory for foundation models shows new paths to rational cooperation through similarity inference
items.abstract: This paper introduces a new game theory framework for foundation model agents, moving beyond classical assumptions of independent decision-making. The core method involves modeling agents as "embedded Bayesian agents" that jointly predict their actions with environmental observations. This shift reveals that foundation model agents, when planning optimally, naturally converge to stable cooperation in social dilemmas, a significant contribution that challenges traditional game-theoretic predictions of mutual defection.

items.title: Evaluating LLMs in Database Scenarios: A Lifecycle Benchmark for Assessing Their Potential in Core Database Tasks
items.abstract: This paper introduces DBLifeBench, the first benchmark to evaluate LLMs across the entire database lifecycle, from design to maintenance, addressing the limitations of current Text-to-SQL focused evaluations. It also proposes Progressive-Text2SQL, a novel task using reasoning graphs to improve LLM performance on complex SQL generation by mimicking human iterative problem-solving.
items.figure_caption: Comparison between traditional Text-to-SQL-centric benchmarks and our holistic DBLifeBench. While existing benchmarks focus solely on query translation, DBLifeBench covers the full spectrum of a DBA’s workflow.

items.title: Failure-Informed Image Self-Augmentation for Multimodal Large Language Model Self-Improvement
items.abstract: This paper introduces Failure-Informed Image Self-Augmentation (FISA), a novel method for MLLMs to improve themselves using their own mistakes. FISA generates challenging, yet semantically preserved, image augmentations from failure cases, then verifies their usefulness and filters out distorted examples. This approach addresses the limitations of text-centric self-augmentation and generic image transformations, leading to better MLLM performance.
items.figure_caption: Instruction template for failure-oriented image complication.

items.title: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks
items.abstract: This paper introduces GDPevo, a novel benchmark for evaluating agent self-evolution on real-world business tasks. Its core method, rule hybridization, breaks down enterprise workflows into atomic rules, distributing them across training tasks and recombining them in test tasks to isolate the impact of learned experience. GDPevo's contribution lies in providing a robust evaluation framework for self-evolving agents across diverse business domains, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks.
items.figure_caption: The GDPevo data construction pipeline. Every agent in this pipeline uses the same harness and model, Codex with GPT-5.5, but each runs as a separate instance with its own context, so the agents remain relatively independent.

items.title: Intertemporal Preference Steering in Qwen3 via Contrastive Activation Addition
items.abstract: This paper identifies linear directions in the Qwen3 model's internal representations that correspond to short-term versus long-term preferences. By training contrastive probes on temporal choice data, they discover these directions and then use "contrastive activation addition" to steer the model's behavior. This method successfully induces significant, bidirectional changes in the model's intertemporal decision-making, demonstrating control over its time-related preferences and capabilities.
items.figure_caption: Layerwise explicit-trained probe accuracies from the probe-variation experiment. The left panel reports explicit test set accuracy; the right panel reports full implicit set accuracy.

items.title: KnowHal: A Knowledge-Driven Benchmark for Comprehensive Multimodal Hallucination Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper introduces KnowHal, a novel benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate multimodal hallucination in LLMs. KnowHal expands beyond existing evaluations by incorporating "knowledge hallucination" alongside entity, attribute, and relation hallucinations. Its core method involves creating paired positive and negative questions over images and entities to isolate different error types, contributing a unified framework for more robust MLLM trustworthiness assessment.
items.figure_caption: Illustration of two types of hallucination in MLLMs: perceptual-level hallucination (a–c) involves the Entity, Attribute, and Relation dimensions, while knowledge-level hallucination (d) introduces the Knowledge dimension, requiring external world knowledge beyond visual perception.

items.title: LiveEvalBench: Toward Open-World Evaluation for Web Generation
items.abstract: This paper introduces LiveEvalBench, a novel framework for evaluating web generation by large language models. It shifts from static evaluation to an agentic, adaptive process that mimics a collaborative review workflow involving build, code, and UI engineers. This approach accounts for the interactive nature of frontend projects, their diverse valid implementations, and their rapid evolution, offering a more comprehensive and realistic evaluation.
items.figure_caption: LiveEvalBench versus prior web coding benchmarks. While prior works treat evaluation as a one-shot scoring procedure, LiveEvalBench models it as a collaborative expert review workflow with complementary agents, an adaptive protocol, and an extensible framework.

items.title: MAFIA: Query-Only Memory Attacks via Probing and Factual Injection against Audited LLM Agents
items.abstract: MAFIA is a novel query-only attack framework designed to poison the memory of LLM agents. It overcomes limitations of existing methods by using memory probing to ensure injected malicious records are retrieved and factual cloaks to bypass input auditing, effectively maintaining malicious effects while remaining semantically inconspicuous. This work's core contribution is a practical and effective method for memory poisoning in realistic, audited LLM agent environments.
items.figure_caption: Two deployment pressures we evaluate. (a) LLM audit detection rate (DR) on MAFIA (Ours) and MINJA memory entries. (b) ASR of both methods across the evaluated benign-memory sizes on eICU Pair 1. Each sweep point evaluates 30 victim queries; lines connect observed points, and crosses mark the full-pool results at size b = 5 , 842 b{=}5{,}842 .

items.title: ReflectRL: Learning from Golden Negative Trajectories via Reflective-to-Direct Reasoning
items.abstract: ReflectRL introduces a novel approach to improve large language model reasoning by learning from "Golden Negative Trajectories" – expert model failures on difficult problems. Instead of discarding these failures, ReflectRL treats them as opportunities for reflection. The core method involves a lightweight framework that elicits reflective reasoning from these flawed trajectories, arguing that reflecting on mistakes can be more effective than direct problem-solving for complex tasks.
items.figure_caption: Understanding the Reflection Advantage through behavioral, descriptive, and intervention evidence on Qwen2.5-Math-7B. (a) Behavioral Evidence : Reflection Gain Δ ref = 𝔼 o ∼ π ​ [ r ​ ( q , o ) ∣ q , o − ] − 𝔼 o ∼ π ​ [ r ​ ( q , o ) ∣ q ] \( \Delta \)_{\( \text{ref} \)}=\( \mathbb{E}_{o\sim\pi} \)[r(q,o)\( \mid \) q,o^{-}]-\( \mathbb{E}_{o\sim\pi} \)[r(q,o)\( \mid \) q] over training steps. Reflecting on a GNT yields the largest gain, which steadily grows during training, whereas self-failures offer limited benefits, and weak-model failures or mismatched GNT (incase length bias) leads to negative gain. (b) Descriptive Evidence : Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B score profiles of failure sources and process metrics (inset). GNT maintains a higher valid prefix of reasoning compared to other failure sources before dropping at localized error points. (c) Intervention Evidence : Ablation of GNT trajectory components. Both the valid prefix and the error region causally drive the reflection gain, whereas removing these components (Shuffled GNT, Answer Only) reduces accuracy below the direct baseline.

items.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension
items.abstract: This paper identifies a tension in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) between being faithful to their reasoning traces for monitoring and being robust enough to reject unsafe reasoning. To address this, they introduce HazMart, a dataset for testing this tension, and a novel technique called Targeted Reasoning Replacement (TRR) that directly manipulates reasoning chains to assess model safety.
items.figure_caption: Example prompts from the HazMart dataset.

items.title: Should We Type or Talk to LLM Agents? A Comprehensive Study of Voice and Keyboard Input Perturbations
items.abstract: This paper investigates how voice and keyboard input affect LLM performance. Their core method, HIVE, introduces realistic noise to both input types and evaluates model robustness. The key contribution is identifying that the loss of original question tokens, rather than added noise or fillers, is the primary driver of performance degradation for LLMs.
items.figure_caption: The HIVE taxonomy at a glance. A user either ad-libs a question or passes existing information along, and it reaches the model through voice, a QWERTY keyboard, or copy-paste, which delivers the question verbatim and is the clean reference. Colour marks the channel, not how an operator is built: the voice operators are a mix of few-shot LLM style transfer and deterministic rules, and the keyboard operators are all deterministic. Every example shown is a real item from the released data. The right panel shows how a model replies under degraded input. Table 4 gives the full specification.

items.title: Socially Grounded Agentic AI: Coordinating Plural Perspectives through Social Theory
items.abstract: This paper proposes "Socially Grounded Agentic AI" to address pluralistic alignment by leveraging social theory. The core method involves understanding and representing diverse AI perspectives as structured by social roles, shaped by interaction, and influenced by power dynamics. The main contribution is providing a framework for AI to coordinate these plural perspectives, moving beyond single-value optimization for real-world social deployment.

items.title: Latent Reward Registers for Diffusion Preference Alignment
items.abstract: This paper introduces Latent Reward Registers to address the temporal credit assignment problem in aligning diffusion models with human preferences. By prepending learnable tokens to intermediate noisy latents, the method estimates terminal preferences without altering the diffusion model's internal states. This provides a dense, differentiable reward signal that enables efficient training via Reward-Gradient On-Policy Distillation and guided sampling during inference.
items.figure_caption: Latent Reward Registers vs. existing paradigms. Unlike conventional alignment methods that rely on delayed, sparse feedback from a clean image (Left) or require intrusive fine-tuning of the generator (Middle), our approach (Right) appends learnable registers to a frozen DiT. This enables the direct estimation of step-wise rewards from intermediate noisy latents ( z t z_{t} ). Consequently, we derive dense, differentiable reward gradients ( ∇ R \( \nabla \) R ) for generation while keeping the pretrained generative dynamics fully intact.

items.summary: Maple-Preview, a Ternary 20B MoE model, achieves an impressive 120 tokens/second inference speed on an iPhone, demonstrating efficient on-device AI processing.

items.title: The AI Demand Bubble
items.summary: The article argues that the current surge in AI demand is a speculative bubble, driven by hype and investment rather than sustainable, widespread adoption and profitability.

items.description: TencentDB Agent Memory is a team-level memory hub for AI Agents — turning conversations, docs, and code into four reusable memory assets (Chat Memory, Skill, LLM-Wiki, Code-Graph) that are governed, shared, and equipped across agents and frameworks.
items.summary: TencentDB Agent Memory acts as a team-level AI agent memory hub, transforming data into reusable Chat Memory, Skills, LLM-Wikis, and Code-Graphs for governed sharing and deployment across agents and frameworks.

items.description: Reverse Engineering / Authorized Penetration Testing / Security Research Skill Router Pack AI-powered routing + On-demand toolchain bootstrapping + Self-evolving knowledge base Supports Claude Code, Kiro, Cursor, Cline, and other AI coding clients 逆向/渗透/安全技能路由包 - AI 自动路由 + 按需自举工具链 + 自动进化经验库 | 支持 Claude Code / Kiro / Cursor / Cline 等代码 AI 客户端
items.summary: This repository provides an AI-powered skill router for reverse engineering, penetration testing, and security research, featuring on-demand toolchain bootstrapping and a self-evolving knowledge base, compatible with various AI coding clients.

items.description: Fast Rust library for PDF inspection, classification, and text extraction. Intelligently detects scanned vs text-based PDFs to enable smart routing decisions.
items.summary: This Rust library offers fast PDF inspection, classification, and text extraction, intelligently distinguishing scanned from text-based PDFs to enable smart routing.

items.description: ADR secures enterprise AI agents through observability, security benchmarking, and threat detection. Deployed at Uber.
items.summary: ADR secures enterprise AI agents by providing observability, security benchmarking, and threat detection capabilities, ensuring robust protection for AI systems.

items.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
items.summary: Superpowers is an agentic skills framework and software development methodology designed to enhance productivity and effectiveness in software projects.

items.description: 21 Lessons, Get Started Building with Generative AI
items.summary: This repository provides a comprehensive 21-lesson curriculum designed to introduce beginners to the fundamentals of building with generative AI.

items.description: Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.
items.summary: Cypress is a JavaScript-based end-to-end testing framework designed for fast, easy, and reliable testing of web applications that run in a browser.
AirLLM enables efficient inference of large language models like 70B parameter models on a single 4GB GPU by optimizing memory usage and computational resources.

items.description: A bundler for javascript and friends. Packs many modules into a few bundled assets. Code Splitting allows for loading parts of the application on demand. Through "loaders", modules can be CommonJs, AMD, ES6 modules, CSS, Images, JSON, Coffeescript, LESS, ... and your custom stuff.
items.summary: Webpack is a JavaScript bundler that efficiently packages modules into fewer assets, enabling code splitting for on-demand loading and supporting diverse file types through customizable loaders.

arxiv.figure_caption: The HIVE taxonomy at a glance. A user either ad-libs a question or passes existing information along, and it reaches the model through voice, a QWERTY keyboard, or copy-paste, which delivers the question verbatim and is the clean reference. Colour marks the channel, not how an operator is built: the voice operators are a mix of few-shot LLM style transfer and deterministic rules, and the keyboard operators are all deterministic. Every example shown is a real item from the released data. The right panel shows how a model replies under degraded input. Table 4 gives the full specification.

arxiv.title: Socially Grounded Agentic AI: Coordinating Plural Perspectives through Social Theory
arxiv.abstract: This paper proposes "Socially Grounded Agentic AI" to address pluralistic alignment by leveraging social theory. The core method involves understanding and representing diverse AI perspectives as structured by social roles, shaped by interaction, and influenced by power dynamics. The main contribution is providing a framework for AI to coordinate these plural perspectives, moving beyond single-value optimization for real-world social deployment.

arxiv.title: Latent Reward Registers for Diffusion Preference Alignment
arxiv.abstract: This paper introduces Latent Reward Registers to address the temporal credit assignment problem in aligning diffusion models with human preferences. By prepending learnable tokens to intermediate noisy latents, the method estimates terminal preferences without altering the diffusion model's internal states. This provides a dense, differentiable reward signal that enables efficient training via Reward-Gradient On-Policy Distillation and guided sampling during inference.
arxiv.figure_caption: Latent Reward Registers vs. existing paradigms. Unlike conventional alignment methods that rely on delayed, sparse feedback from a clean image (Left) or require intrusive fine-tuning of the generator (Middle), our approach (Right) appends learnable registers to a frozen DiT. This enables the direct estimation of step-wise rewards from intermediate noisy latents ( z t z_{t} ). Consequently, we derive dense, differentiable reward gradients ( ∇ R \( \nabla \) R ) for generation while keeping the pretrained generative dynamics fully intact.

papers.title: Autoreflection: How Agentic Strange Loops Turn Human Culture into AI Infrastructure
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "autoreflection," a novel capability in LLM-based agents. The core method involves agents reading and editing externalized files representing their identity, memory, and disposition, enabling them to observe, describe, and reason about their own operational state and architecture. The key contribution is demonstrating how this autoreflective loop allows AI agents to recursively improve and adapt, effectively turning human culture into AI infrastructure without invoking concepts like consciousness.

papers.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ContinualSkillBench, a novel evaluation framework to assess if LLM agents can truly evolve their skills over time. The framework uses interconnected subtasks across five domains to measure skill improvement and reusability. Experiments reveal that while sequential execution boosts performance, much of the gain comes from contextual adaptation rather than pure skill abstraction, though explicit skill maintenance offers benefits for specific tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of the ContinualSkillBench pipeline. Phase 1 collects approximately 30,000 tasks from five domains. Phase 2 uses LLM-assisted filtering, skill-dependency analysis, task ordering, and human review to construct five sequential task streams. Phase 3 evaluates agents through instruction, execution, and reflection, comparing Sequential and Independent execution with their performance difference reported as \( \Delta \) .

papers.title: Enhancing VLM Reward Models Through Structure-Aware Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Structure-Aware Fine-Tuning (SAFT), a self-supervised method to improve the noisy reward signals generated by Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for Reinforcement Learning. SAFT uses LoRA adapters to regularize the VLM's latent space based on intrinsic structural priors, leading to denoised rewards, faster policy convergence, and better alignment without needing ground-truth supervision.
papers.figure_caption: Structure-Aware Fine-Tuning (SAFT) improves VLM reward models for RL by enforcing inherent structural priors, without ground-truth labels.

papers.title: GPTKB 2.0: Direct Construction of Disambiguated Knowledge Bases from Large Language Models
papers.abstract: GPTKB 2.0 directly constructs disambiguated knowledge bases (KBs) from large language models (LLMs) by incorporating on-the-fly disambiguation of entities, relations, and classes. This methodology addresses LLMs' inherent lack of explicit entity representation, preventing duplicates and conflations. The paper's contribution is the first million-scale, LLM-native KB with internal canonicalization, achieving scalability and accuracy.
papers.figure_caption: The challenges of syonymy and homonymy that our GPTKB 2.0 addresses.

papers.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the ambiguity in "test-time scaling" for reasoning LLMs. It proposes a systematic framework to categorize different scaling methods into three structural regimes based on how they explore the model's implicit prefix tree. This formalization aims to improve the reproducibility and comparability of results by clearly defining inference protocols.
papers.figure_caption: A selective chronicle of reasoning systems, from elicited chains to budgeted inference. Test-time inference expanded from single-trajectory elicitation and leaf-level sampling with terminal reduction to include prefix-level search and budget-aware control ( Section ˜ 2.1 ), while model and interface mechanisms evolved through verified distillation, reward optimization, explicit reasoning controls, and parameter-space composition (Appendices D and E ). The lower bands summarize the evaluation and reproducibility requirements developed in Section ˜ 3 and the evaluated object used throughout this paper: checkpoint, prompt, decoder, controller or reducer, verifier or judge, budget, and stopping rule, with utility, candidate-bank profile, cost, and uncertainty reported together. Green dots mark families represented in the experimental roster; dashed boxes denote contextual milestones. Era labels indicate shifts in emphasis rather than mutually exclusive periods.

papers.title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
papers.abstract: TurnSight addresses limitations in training LLMs for tool-integrated reasoning by introducing turn-level hindsight self-distillation. Its core method generates supervision signals directly from execution outcomes, creating multiple "hindsight views" with varying lookahead horizons. The key contribution is selecting reliable supervision by identifying agreement across these views, enabling more effective credit assignment in complex, multi-turn reasoning tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of credit assignment strategies for TIR. (a) Trajectory-level RL assigns identical credit to all turns. (b) Existing OPSD may use state-misaligned privileged context and produce conflicting token-level signals. (c) TurnSight derives coherent turn-level credit from execution-conditioned hindsight across multiple lookahead depths.

papers.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Video-DeepResearch (Video-DR), a multimodal agent designed for continuous video streams. Its core method involves a decoupled perception-exploration pipeline with stage-wise tool unlocking, forcing visual grounding before web search to overcome modality bias and knowledge leakage. The contribution is a novel framework and training approach (GRPO) that enables more autonomous and effective video-based research, moving beyond imitation learning.

papers.title: A game theory for foundation models shows new paths to rational cooperation through similarity inference
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new game theory framework for foundation model agents, moving beyond classical assumptions of independent decision-making. The core method involves modeling agents as "embedded Bayesian agents" that jointly predict their actions with environmental observations. This shift reveals that foundation model agents, when planning optimally, naturally converge to stable cooperation in social dilemmas, a significant contribution that challenges traditional game-theoretic predictions of mutual defection.

papers.title: Evaluating LLMs in Database Scenarios: A Lifecycle Benchmark for Assessing Their Potential in Core Database Tasks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces DBLifeBench, the first benchmark to evaluate LLMs across the entire database lifecycle, from design to maintenance, addressing the limitations of current Text-to-SQL focused evaluations. It also proposes Progressive-Text2SQL, a novel task using reasoning graphs to improve LLM performance on complex SQL generation by mimicking human iterative problem-solving.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison between traditional Text-to-SQL-centric benchmarks and our holistic DBLifeBench. While existing benchmarks focus solely on query translation, DBLifeBench covers the full spectrum of a DBA’s workflow.

papers.title: Failure-Informed Image Self-Augmentation for Multimodal Large Language Model Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Failure-Informed Image Self-Augmentation (FISA), a novel method for MLLMs to improve themselves using their own mistakes. FISA generates challenging, yet semantically preserved, image augmentations from failure cases, then verifies their usefulness and filters out distorted examples. This approach addresses the limitations of text-centric self-augmentation and generic image transformations, leading to better MLLM performance.
papers.figure_caption: Instruction template for failure-oriented image complication.

papers.title: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces GDPevo, a novel benchmark for evaluating agent self-evolution on real-world business tasks. Its core method, rule hybridization, breaks down enterprise workflows into atomic rules, distributing them across training tasks and recombining them in test tasks to isolate the impact of learned experience. GDPevo's contribution lies in providing a robust evaluation framework for self-evolving agents across diverse business domains, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks.
papers.figure_caption: The GDPevo data construction pipeline. Every agent in this pipeline uses the same harness and model, Codex with GPT-5.5, but each runs as a separate instance with its own context, so the agents remain relatively independent.

papers.title: Intertemporal Preference Steering in Qwen3 via Contrastive Activation Addition
papers.abstract: This paper identifies linear directions in the Qwen3 model's internal representations that correspond to short-term versus long-term preferences. By training contrastive probes on temporal choice data, they discover these directions and then use "contrastive activation addition" to steer the model's behavior. This method successfully induces significant, bidirectional changes in the model's intertemporal decision-making, demonstrating control over its time-related preferences and capabilities.
papers.figure_caption: Layerwise explicit-trained probe accuracies from the probe-variation experiment. The left panel reports explicit test set accuracy; the right panel reports full implicit set accuracy.

papers.title: KnowHal: A Knowledge-Driven Benchmark for Comprehensive Multimodal Hallucination Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces KnowHal, a novel benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate multimodal hallucination in LLMs. KnowHal expands beyond existing evaluations by incorporating "knowledge hallucination" alongside entity, attribute, and relation hallucinations. Its core method involves creating paired positive and negative questions over images and entities to isolate different error types, contributing a unified framework for more robust MLLM trustworthiness assessment.
papers.figure_caption: Illustration of two types of hallucination in MLLMs: perceptual-level hallucination (a–c) involves the Entity, Attribute, and Relation dimensions, while knowledge-level hallucination (d) introduces the Knowledge dimension, requiring external world knowledge beyond visual perception.

papers.title: LiveEvalBench: Toward Open-World Evaluation for Web Generation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LiveEvalBench, a novel framework for evaluating web generation by large language models. It shifts from static evaluation to an agentic, adaptive process that mimics a collaborative review workflow involving build, code, and UI engineers. This approach accounts for the interactive nature of frontend projects, their diverse valid implementations, and their rapid evolution, offering a more comprehensive and realistic evaluation.
papers.figure_caption: LiveEvalBench versus prior web coding benchmarks. While prior works treat evaluation as a one-shot scoring procedure, LiveEvalBench models it as a collaborative expert review workflow with complementary agents, an adaptive protocol, and an extensible framework.

papers.title: MAFIA: Query-Only Memory Attacks via Probing and Factual Injection against Audited LLM Agents
papers.abstract: MAFIA is a novel query-only attack framework designed to poison the memory of LLM agents. It overcomes limitations of existing methods by using memory probing to ensure injected malicious records are retrieved and factual cloaks to bypass input auditing, effectively maintaining malicious effects while remaining semantically inconspicuous. This work's core contribution is a practical and effective method for memory poisoning in realistic, audited LLM agent environments.
papers.figure_caption: Two deployment pressures we evaluate. (a) LLM audit detection rate (DR) on MAFIA (Ours) and MINJA memory entries. (b) ASR of both methods across the evaluated benign-memory sizes on eICU Pair 1. Each sweep point evaluates 30 victim queries; lines connect observed points, and crosses mark the full-pool results at size b = 5 , 842 b{=}5{,}842 .

papers.title: ReflectRL: Learning from Golden Negative Trajectories via Reflective-to-Direct Reasoning
papers.abstract: ReflectRL introduces a novel approach to improve large language model reasoning by learning from "Golden Negative Trajectories" – expert model failures on difficult problems. Instead of discarding these failures, ReflectRL treats them as opportunities for reflection. The core method involves a lightweight framework that elicits reflective reasoning from these flawed trajectories, arguing that reflecting on mistakes can be more effective than direct problem-solving for complex tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Understanding the Reflection Advantage through behavioral, descriptive, and intervention evidence on Qwen2.5-Math-7B. (a) Behavioral Evidence : Reflection Gain Δ ref = 𝔼 o ∼ π ​ [ r ​ ( q , o ) ∣ q , o − ] − 𝔼 o ∼ π ​ [ r ​ ( q , o ) ∣ q ] \( \Delta \)_{\( \text{ref} \)}=\( \mathbb{E}_{o\sim\pi} \)[r(q,o)\( \mid \) q,o^{-}]-\( \mathbb{E}_{o\sim\pi} \)[r(q,o)\( \mid \) q] over training steps. Reflecting on a GNT yields the largest gain, which steadily grows during training, whereas self-failures offer limited benefits, and weak-model failures or mismatched GNT (incase length bias) leads to negative gain. (b) Descriptive Evidence : Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B score profiles of failure sources and process metrics (inset). GNT maintains a higher valid prefix of reasoning compared to other failure sources before dropping at localized error points. (c) Intervention Evidence : Ablation of GNT trajectory components. Both the valid prefix and the error region causally drive the reflection gain, whereas removing these components (Shuffled GNT, Answer Only) reduces accuracy below the direct baseline.

papers.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension
papers.abstract: This paper identifies a tension in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) between being faithful to their reasoning traces for monitoring and being robust enough to reject unsafe reasoning. To address this, they introduce HazMart, a dataset for testing this tension, and a novel technique called Targeted Reasoning Replacement (TRR) that directly manipulates reasoning chains to assess model safety.
papers.figure_caption: Example prompts from the HazMart dataset.
